chunks: A group informed me of it, from Abū Muḥammad Hārūn ibn Mūsā, from Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Awdī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “If the woman and the bondwoman experience sexual desire, whether a man had intercourse with her or did not have intercourse with her, whether that occurred in sleep or in wakefulness, then ghusl (ritual bath) is obligatory upon her.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the speaker of the hadith
key_terms.الْأَمَةُ: a bondwoman or female slave, included in the same ruling
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: ghusl (ritual bath), the obligatory purification mentioned here
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: a free woman, addressed here in the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl (ritual bath) become obligatory for a woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning janabah and the obligation of ghusl (ritual bath) for a woman or bondwoman when sexual pleasure occurs. It indicates that the ruling applies regardless of whether this happened during sleep or wakefulness, making it part of the fiqh of ritual purity.
